summary: Answers a question about the codebase by splitting it into areas, researching them with parallel sub-agents, and writing one evidence-backed research.md into a change folder.

nodes.title: Take in the question and named files
nodes.concept: Anything the user pointed at is read in full by the main agent first, so its own context holds the ground truth before anything is delegated.

nodes.title: Load accepted lessons as priors
nodes.concept: lessons.md holds rules the team already agreed on. Reading it up front narrows what is worth re-investigating instead of rediscovering known pitfalls.

nodes.title: Split the question into research areas
nodes.concept: A broad question becomes a few independent areas. Each area later becomes one sub-agent's assignment, so the split decides the shape of the whole run.

nodes.title: Agree on depth and focus with you
nodes.concept: A cheap question before an expensive fan-out. Depth and focus change how many agents run and what they read, so the skill pins them down first.
nodes.when: the question is broad or ambiguous; tight queries skip this gate

nodes.title: Research areas in parallel
nodes.concept: 2–4 sub-agents (fast Explore for finding, general-purpose for deep reading) work at once. Each keeps its own context, so the main agent only receives findings with file:line references.

nodes.title: Trace the live code
nodes.concept: Current code is the primary source of truth; these agents map files, entry points and data flow.

nodes.title: Mine prior changes for decisions
nodes.concept: context/changes and context/archive explain why the code looks the way it does. This is supplementary history, never a substitute for the code.

nodes.title: Wait for every agent, then connect findings
nodes.concept: The barrier matters: synthesis starts only when all agents are done, so cross-area connections are made with the full picture, live code ranked above history.

nodes.title: Resolve the change folder and metadata
nodes.concept: Research belongs to a change. The skill reuses or creates context/changes/<id>/, refuses archived ones, and gathers commit, branch and date so the document has no placeholders.

nodes.title: Write research.md
nodes.concept: One fixed template (frontmatter, summary, detailed findings, code references, history, open questions) makes every research doc comparable and consumable by /10x-plan.

nodes.title: Swap local refs for GitHub permalinks
nodes.concept: Permalinks pin each reference to a commit, so links stay valid after the code moves on.
nodes.when: on main/master or the commit is pushed

nodes.title: Present findings and invite follow-ups
nodes.concept: A short summary with key references closes the loop; follow-up questions append to the same document instead of starting over.
